title: Enterprise Supply Chain and Build Readiness v1 — Rig Relay

gaps: No NPM lockfile (frontend assets not tracked here)
dependency_pinning_strategy.recommendation: Verify any JS/CSS dependencies are also pinned.

evidence: exclude-newer = 7 days prevents supply-chain attacks via new releases
uv_lockfile_status.recommendation: Continue current practice. Periodically audit lockfile for stale/compromised packages.

gaps: No automated license compatibility check of all 50+ direct dependencies
No license change detection in CI
AGPL is the most restrictive open-source license. Many enterprises have blanket AGPL prohibitions.
Upstream mistral-vibe was Apache 2.0 — the transition to AGPL needs clear documentation of what changed and why.
license_compatibility.recommendation: Add license scanning to CI (e.g., licensecheck or pip-licenses). Produce full dependency license inventory. Document AGPL choice rationale. Offer commercial license for enterprises with AGPL restrictions.

agpl_commercial_implications.issue: AGPL-3.0 requires that all users who interact with the software over a network receive access to the complete source code. For a developer tool that may become a hosted service, this creates significant enterprise adoption friction.
enterprise_concerns: Enterprises with no-AGPL policies will automatically reject
AGPL's network-use clause may apply to hosted deployments
Contributor License Agreement (CLA) required in CONTRIBUTING.md adds friction for open-source contributors
Commercial/enterprise licensing path not yet defined
agpl_commercial_implications.recommendation: Define dual-licensing strategy (AGPL + commercial). Create commercial license terms. Address AGPL FUD proactively in procurement docs.

sbom_readiness.recommendation: Use pip-audit or syft to generate SPDX SBOM from uv.lock. Publish SBOM with each release. Validate SBOM against schema in CI. Add SBOM link to README and security page.

gaps: No dependency vulnerability scanning (pip-audit, safety, or OSV-Scanner)
No Dependabot or Renovate for automated updates
vulnerability_scanning_readiness.recommendation: Add pip-audit to CI. Configure Dependabot for Python dependencies. Set up GitHub Security Advisory notifications. Define vulnerability response SLA.

evidence: 7 workflow files (ci.yml, release.yml, codeql.yml, codeql-swift-advisory.yml, build-and-upload.yml, pages.yml, issue-labeler.yml)
All actions pinned by commit SHA
Schema validation, site renderer, release gate, CodeQL in CI
gaps: No required reviewers configured (may exist but not confirmed)
github_actions_status.recommendation: Verify and document branch protection rules. Add Dependabot for GitHub Actions.

gaps: No cryptographic signing of release artifacts
No checksum publication for releases (manifest exists but not signed)
PyPI publishing uses trusted publishing (OIDC) — good but not sufficient alone
artifact_signing_and_provenance.recommendation: Implement SLSA L2 provenance using slsa-github-generator. Sign release artifacts with cosign. Publish SHA256 checksums with each release. Verify provenance in CI.

evidence: PyInstaller builds for 5 platforms (linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, darwin-x86_64, darwin-aarch64, windows-x86_64)
release_packaging.recommendation: Add macOS notarization. Add Windows signing. Consider Flatpak/AppImage for Linux distribution.

gaps: No automatic update delivery for binary distributions
update_mechanism.recommendation: Implement signed update delivery. Add update channels. Verify update signatures before applying.

evidence: CI builds are scripted and repeatable
reproducibility_evidence.recommendation: Work toward reproducible builds. Document build environment. Compare CI builds across runs.

evidence: Dependency policy with 3-bucket model (core runtime, workbench/dev, optional extras)
Core dependencies justified in dependency policy
gaps: No automated dependency review in PRs
No policy for adding new core dependencies
dependency_review_policy.recommendation: Add dependency review GitHub Action. Schedule quarterly dependency audits. Document new dependency approval process.

findings: google-api-python-client brings heavy transitive dependency chain (google-auth, uritemplate, etc.)
pywebview is platform-specific and brings platform-native dependencies
tree-sitter-* packages are prebuilt binaries — supply-chain risk for binary artifacts
mistralai==2.4.4 is pinned to exact version — legacy dependency from upstream fork
agent-client-protocol==0.9.0 is pinned — alpha protocol dependency
vendored_and_transitive_risks.recommendation: Audit transitive dependency licenses. Verify tree-sitter binary provenance. Plan mistralai deprecation if no longer needed. Document binary dependency policy.

evidence: Static site generated from JSON source via renderer
No analytics or tracking on site
gaps: Renderer could be compromised to inject content
generated_docs_static_site_risks.recommendation: Add CSP meta tag. Add XSS scan. Pin renderer dependencies. Review rendered output for content injection.

summary.overall_status: Supply-chain posture is solid for alpha-stage local-first tool but insufficient for enterprise procurement. Critical gaps: no SBOM, no dependency vulnerability scanning, no artifact signing, AGPL-only licensing.
